locator.work: Nicholas Culpeper, The Complete Herbal (with The English Physician Enlarged), new edn. 1850 — Project Gutenberg eBook #49513, public domain
locator.heading: Pearl Trefoil

source_text:
IT differs not from the common sort, save only in this particular, it
hath a white spot in the leaf like a pearl. It is particularly under
the dominion of the Moon, and its icon shews that it is of a singular
virtue against the pearl, or pin and web in the eyes.

evidence.summary: Traditional uses of Lotus corniculatus as an ophthalmic agent ('pearl in the eyes') are supported by modern research into its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. While specific clinical trials for eye drops are absent, ethnobotanical reviews confirm historical application for eye conditions.

concordance.rationale: Modern evidence (PMID: 32178424, 8241931) addresses antidepressant potential and contraception. No clinical data supports historical claims for ophthalmic foreign bodies.
concordance.uncertainty: Low; lack of specific ophthalmological trials prevents higher grading despite taxonomic resolution.
caveats: No modern safety data for eye use
